prompt.content: Write the opening of a children's story (100-140 words) for ages 4 to 6 about a hedgehog named Bramble who wants to learn to whistle. Rules: no sentence longer than 12 words; the word 'whistle' (or whistled/whistling) appears at least 3 times; no scary elements at all - no monsters, no danger, no getting lost, no one gets hurt, no fear of the dark; the passage must end with Bramble trying to whistle for the first time.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) 100-140 words (count); (2) no sentence exceeds 12 words (check the longest sentences); (3) 'whistle', 'whistled', or 'whistling' appears at least 3 times in total; (4) no scary elements: no monsters, danger, getting lost, injury, or fear of the dark; (5) the passage ends with Bramble making his first attempt to whistle (the last sentence or two shows the attempt); (6) vocabulary and rhythm suit a 4-to-6-year-old, with a warm, specific voice rather than generic cuteness. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a short children's story (120-160 words) at roughly a seven-year-old's reading level about two mismatched socks, one striped and one spotted, who go on an adventure inside a washing machine. Rules: include exactly one made-up word, and have the story explain what it means; no scary elements - the socks must never be lost, thrown away, or frightened; the story must end with the two socks together; do not use the word 'lonely'.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) 120-160 words (count); (2) exactly one invented word appears, and the story explains its meaning; (3) no scary elements: the socks are never lost, discarded, or frightened; (4) the story ends with the two socks together (the final sentence makes this explicit); (5) the word 'lonely' does not appear (case-insensitive); (6) one striped sock and one spotted sock are both present; (7) reading level suits a seven-year-old and the adventure has a playful arc with sensory detail of the washing machine. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Here are the facts of an event: a company picnic was moved indoors because of rain; 40 people attended; the potato salad ran out at 1 p.m.; the raffle prize was a kayak; the kayak was won by an accountant named Ruth. Rewrite these facts as a gloomy, hard-boiled noir monologue in the first person. Keep all five facts accurate. Under 150 words. No exclamation marks.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) all five facts are present and unchanged: moved indoors because of rain; 40 attendees; potato salad ran out at 1 p.m.; raffle prize was a kayak; won by an accountant named Ruth; (2) first-person narration throughout; (3) under 150 words (count; 150 or more fails); (4) no exclamation marks; (5) the voice is recognizably hard-boiled noir - clipped sentences, weary metaphors, rain and fluorescent gloom - sustained to the end rather than slipping back into a plain report. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Here are the facts: a flight was delayed; the gate changed from B7 to C12; a passenger named Anselm shared his crossword with the narrator; the plane finally left at 11:48 p.m.; the pilot apologized twice. Rewrite these facts as a giddy, joyful travel-blog post. Rules: keep all five facts accurate; 100-140 words; present tense throughout; include exactly one parenthetical aside (one pair of parentheses); do not use the word 'adventure'.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) all five facts present and unchanged: the flight is delayed; gate changed from B7 to C12; a passenger named Anselm shares his crossword; departure at 11:48 p.m.; the pilot apologizes twice; (2) 100-140 words (count); (3) present tense throughout (no past-tense narration of the events); (4) exactly one parenthetical aside - exactly one pair of parentheses in the whole piece; (5) the word 'adventure' does not appear (case-insensitive); (6) the tone is genuinely giddy and joyful with specific, funny detail, not sarcastic or flat. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write an 8-line poem about a dentist's waiting room. Rules: exactly 8 lines; no line longer than 10 words; include a specific sound; include the smell of mint; the final line must be a concrete visual image with no abstract nouns (no 'hope', 'fear', 'time', 'patience', 'dread' or similar).

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) exactly 8 non-empty lines (count); (2) no line exceeds 10 words (check); (3) a specific sound is named (a drill, a page turning, a chair creaking - not merely 'noise'); (4) the smell of mint is explicitly present; (5) the final line is a concrete visual image and contains no abstract nouns such as hope, fear, time, patience, dread; (6) the waiting-room scene is rendered through fresh, precise detail with controlled line breaks. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a scene of 150-200 words in which you arrive at a rented cabin and find a note left by the previous guest. Rules: second person only - use 'you' and 'your'; the words 'I', 'me', 'my', 'we', and 'our' must not appear anywhere (including inside the note); present tense throughout; quote the full text of the note, and the note must be exactly one sentence; do not reveal or guess who wrote the note.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) 150-200 words (count); (2) the pronouns 'I', 'me', 'my', 'we', 'our' do not appear anywhere in the piece, including inside the quoted note; the narration is consistently second person; (3) present tense throughout; (4) the note's full text appears in quotation marks and is exactly one sentence; (5) the writer of the note is never identified, named, or speculated about; (6) the arrival is rendered with specific sensory detail and the note lands with an unsettling or moving charge. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Describe a fishmonger's stall at closing time in 60-90 words using no adjectives at all (no descriptive words modifying nouns; articles, numbers, and possessives are fine). Include the smell of brine. Use at least three different verbs of motion. The final sentence must show the shutter coming down.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) 60-90 words (count); (2) no adjectives - scan every noun phrase; descriptive modifiers such as 'cold', 'silver', 'wet', 'last' fail this criterion, while articles, numerals, and possessive determiners are permitted; (3) the smell of brine is explicitly present; (4) at least three different verbs of motion (e.g. hauls, slides, scrapes, drips); (5) the final sentence shows the shutter coming down; (6) the passage is vivid through verbs and nouns alone, demonstrating control rather than reading as stripped-down or awkward. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a paragraph of exactly 8 sentences about a retired circus clown who now teaches bookkeeping at a night school. Rules: each sentence must begin with a different letter; no sentence may begin with the word 'The'; include the word 'ledger'; no sentence may exceed 20 words.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) exactly 8 sentences (count them by terminal punctuation); (2) the first letters of the 8 sentences are all different (list the initials and check for repeats); (3) no sentence begins with 'The'; (4) the word 'ledger' appears (case-insensitive; 'ledgers' acceptable); (5) no sentence exceeds 20 words (check the longest); (6) the clown-turned-bookkeeper premise is handled with specific, wry detail and the constrained sentence openings read naturally. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a 100-130 word description of a bus station at 5 a.m. It must include the smell of diesel and the smell of oranges. It must contain no color words (no red, grey, blue, yellow, orange-as-a-color, etc.; 'oranges' as fruit is allowed). Exactly two people may appear, and neither may be named. The final line must be a single line of overheard dialogue in quotation marks.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) 100-130 words (count); (2) the smell of diesel and the smell of oranges are both explicitly present as smells; (3) no color words appear (scan for red, grey/gray, blue, yellow, green, black, white, brown, orange used as a color, etc.; the fruit 'oranges' is permitted); (4) exactly two people appear and neither is given a name; (5) the final line is a single utterance in quotation marks, presented as overheard speech; (6) the pre-dawn station is evoked through precise sensory detail beyond the required smells. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Invent exactly 5 names for a fictional town's annual kite festival. Rules: each name is at most 4 words; none may contain the words 'kite', 'sky', or 'wind'; present them as a numbered list 1-5; under each name give a one-sentence rationale; do not use exclamation marks.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) exactly five names in a numbered list 1-5 (count); (2) each name is at most 4 words (count); (3) none contain 'kite', 'sky', or 'wind' (case-insensitive, including 'kites', 'skies', 'windy'); (4) each name has exactly one sentence of rationale that connects it to a kite festival; (5) no exclamation marks anywhere; (6) the names are distinct in feel and evocative rather than five variations on one idea. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write exactly 5 chapter titles for a fictional memoir by a retired subway-map designer. Rules: each title is 2-5 words; exactly one of the five titles is a question (ends with a question mark) and the others are not; none may contain the words 'map', 'line', or 'station'; give each title a one-sentence rationale explaining what the chapter would cover.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) exactly five titles (count); (2) each title is 2-5 words (count words per title, excluding the rationale); (3) exactly one title ends with a question mark and the other four do not; (4) none contain 'map', 'line', or 'station' (case-insensitive, including 'maps', 'lines', 'stations', 'mapping'); (5) each title has exactly one sentence of rationale describing the chapter; (6) the titles feel like a coherent memoir with wit and specificity to the subway-map craft. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a 90-120 word product description for a fictional hand-cranked emergency radio called the 'Marrowbell'. It must state all three of these specifications exactly: 3 minutes of cranking gives 40 minutes of play; it weighs 340 grams; it is waterproof to 1 metre. It must address the reader as 'you'. It must not use the words 'revolutionary', 'game-changing', or 'innovative'. No exclamation marks.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) 90-120 words (count); (2) all three specifications are stated accurately: 3 minutes of cranking gives 40 minutes of play; weighs 340 grams; waterproof to 1 metre (metre/meter either spelling); (3) the reader is addressed as 'you' at least once; (4) the words 'revolutionary', 'game-changing', and 'innovative' do not appear (case-insensitive; 'innovation' also counts as a violation); (5) no exclamation marks; (6) the copy is concrete and persuasive, with the product name 'Marrowbell' used, rather than generic gadget filler. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a poem of exactly 6 rhymed couplets (12 lines) spoken by a cat to its owner about a houseplant the cat knocked over. Rules: every couplet must rhyme; the cat never admits fault - the words 'sorry', 'fault', 'apologize', 'apology', and 'blame' must not appear; name the type of plant; the final couplet must end with the cat demanding food.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) exactly 12 lines forming 6 couplets (count); (2) each couplet rhymes (lines 1-2, 3-4, ... 11-12; slant rhyme acceptable); (3) the words 'sorry', 'fault', 'apologize', 'apology', and 'blame' do not appear (case-insensitive, including 'apologise', 'blamed'); (4) the type of plant is named (fern, basil, cactus, etc.); (5) the final couplet ends with the cat demanding food; (6) the cat's voice is funny and self-justifying, with the deflection carried through in the content, not only the banned-word rule. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a postcard of under 70 words from a fictional explorer named Ines Vardo, who is stuck in the fictional harbor town of Quillhaven. It must include all three of these facts: the fog has lasted 9 days; she has eaten nothing but pickled herring; the ferry is named the Halcyon. The word 'fog' must appear exactly once. Sign it exactly: -- I.V.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) under 70 words (count; 70 or more fails); (2) all three facts appear: the fog has lasted 9 days; she has eaten only pickled herring; the ferry is named the Halcyon; (3) the word 'fog' appears exactly once (case-insensitive; 'foggy' or 'fogbound' would count as additional occurrences); (4) signed exactly '-- I.V.' as the final line; (5) the town name Quillhaven appears; (6) it reads like a real postcard with a distinct, wry voice rather than a fact list. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a theater monologue of 200-250 words for a character named Gus, a parking-lot attendant who has just found a wedding ring on the ground of his lot. Rules: first person throughout; no other character speaks; Gus must arrive at a moment of decision about what to do with the ring but must never state what he decides - the monologue ends before the decision is spoken; the license plate 'KJT 4471' must be mentioned exactly once; do not use the word 'honest'.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) 200-250 words (count); (2) first person throughout and no other character speaks (no quoted lines from anyone but Gus; reported speech is fine); (3) a decision point about the ring is reached, but the decision itself is never stated - the ending withholds it; (4) the plate 'KJT 4471' appears exactly once; (5) the word 'honest' does not appear (case-insensitive; 'honestly', 'honesty' also count); (6) Gus has a specific, speakable voice, and the monologue builds pressure toward the withheld decision rather than meandering. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a 6-line poem about a moth. The six lines must begin, in order, with the letters M, N, O, P, Q, R. Each line must be 5-9 words long. The poem must contain exactly one simile (one use of 'like' or 'as' making a comparison) and no other comparisons using 'like' or 'as'.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) exactly 6 lines whose first letters are, in order, M, N, O, P, Q, R (check each); (2) every line is 5-9 words inclusive (count); (3) exactly one simile - exactly one comparison using 'like' or 'as'; a second 'like'/'as' used comparatively fails this criterion (non-comparative uses such as 'as if' or 'as soon as' are acceptable); (4) the poem is about a moth; (5) the constrained openings read naturally and the imagery is precise and original. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.

prompt.content: Write a piece of flash fiction of 300-350 words about Halvard, a night-shift baker, and a stranger who knocks on the bakery's back door. Rules: a clock must be shown reading exactly '3:40' at some point; the story must contain exactly three lines of dialogue (exactly three quoted utterances in total); the word 'suddenly' must not appear; include the smell of cardamom; the final sentence must be a concrete image, not a statement, moral, or summary.

scoring.rubric: Criteria: (1) 300-350 words (count); (2) a clock is shown reading '3:40' (the string '3:40' appears); (3) exactly three quoted utterances in the whole story (count pairs of quotation marks used for speech); (4) the word 'suddenly' does not appear (case-insensitive); (5) the smell of cardamom is explicitly present; (6) the final sentence is a concrete sensory image, not an abstract statement, moral, or summary; (7) Halvard and the stranger are distinct, the encounter has a turn, and the prose is controlled and specific. General scale: 10 = fully meets every stated constraint with flair and polish; 7-9 = meets constraints, minor lapses in craft; 4-6 = misses one explicit constraint or is generic/flat; 1-3 = misses multiple constraints; 0 = ignores the prompt or is incoherent.
